title: Answer incoming calls in the browser with ring groups
summary: Route a number or your default route to a ring group, and incoming calls ring its online members in the dashboard phone until one answers.
body_markdown:
Your team can now answer incoming calls in the[browser phone](https://bird.com/docs/guides/voice/phone) . Choose **Online** in the dashboard phone, and a call for one of your **ring groups** rings with the ringtone you picked and shows a system notification with the caller's number and contact name. The first member to select **Accept** takes the call, and it stops ringing for everyone else. Choose **Busy** to keep placing calls without being rung.


Every workspace starts with a **Default** group that rings everyone online. Add your own, such as support or sales, and point a number or your workspace's default inbound route at the group that should answer it. Members are rung five at a time until one of them answers, and after three missed calls in a row the phone stops ringing that member until they choose **Back online** .


Manage groups from **Voice → Ring groups** in the dashboard, or through the API, SDKs, CLI (` bird voice ring-groups` ), and MCP:[create a group](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/create-voice-ring-group) and[add members](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/create-voice-ring-group-member) by user ID, then set a number's or the workspace's route` type` to` ring_group` (see[update a number](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/update-voice-number) and[update voice settings](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/update-voice-settings) ). A workspace can have up to 50 groups beyond the default, each with up to 200 members. See the[ring groups guide](https://bird.com/docs/guides/voice/ring-groups) for the full walkthrough.


Also in this release:


- **Email template personalization isn't just for broadcasts anymore.** An individual, batch, or scheduled send can now use` {{ bird.contact.* }}` placeholders: Bird looks up each To address's contact in your workspace, and Cc/Bcc recipients receive a personalized copy for every To. A To with no matching contact rejects the send with` 422` (` E04099` ). See[personalizing with variables](https://bird.com/docs/guides/email/templates#personalizing-with-variables) and[create an email message](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/create-email-message) .
- **Broadcast templates can loop again.** A broadcast template can now use` {% for %}` over a local list built with` split` , and, when it takes no caller parameters, literal ranges and` {% tablerow %}` too. Broadcast parameters stay scalar-only; arrays and objects still aren't supported.
- **Large files can upload to the media library in the background.** New[asset upload session](https://bird.com/docs/api/reference/create-asset-upload-session) endpoints let a client transfer bytes directly to temporary storage and complete the upload asynchronously, instead of a single multipart request, with sessions capped per workspace and organization.
- **SMS and WhatsApp message history masks sensitive template values instead of fully redacting them.** A one-time code sent through a system template now reads with one asterisk per digit in its surrounding text; only authentication messages without declared sensitive variables still read` **REDACTED**` .
